WHEREAS, the Pacifica School District (the 'District") is determined to provide a quality
well-rounded publiO education and believes having a great teacher in each classroom is the most

WHEREAS, nationally, California places near the bottom of the 50 states in educaüonal

WHEREAS, it is essential the Disfrict have stable, reliable local funding to maintain and

WI-m-EAS, having a quality teacher in each classroom is one of the most important

WHEREAS, the District acknowledges the importance of paying teachers and
staff a living wage so they can cond.nue to live in the community where they work; and
WHEREAS, to better attact and retain excellent teachers and other school educational

all money raised by this measure will go to the Distict's local schools, and
cannot be taken away by the State; and
WHEREAS, even if voters do not have school-age children, supporting quality education
is a wise investment since good schools improve the quality of life in the Pacifica community and
protect the value of our homes; and
WHEREAS, on June 7, 2016, Pacifica voters renewed a school parcel tax measure

WHEREAS, the existing parcel tax authorized by Measure D will expire as of June 30,
WHEREAS, 4 0fArtic1e A and Section 2(d) 0fArtic1eX111 C ofthe California

Section 50079 authorizes a school disfrict to impose qualified special taxes meeting certain

WHEREAS, all funds raised in these qualified special taxes are spent for the benefit of
studenß residing in our District; and
WHEREAS, Section 1000 of the California Elections Code authorizes the District to
conduct such an only on an established elecfion date; and
WI-EREAS, November 3, 2026, is an established election date; and
WHEREAS, this Board of Trustees has held a public hearing after due notice regarding the
parcel tax proposed by this as required by California Government Code 50077;
and
WI-IEREAS, the Distict is located entirely within the County ofSan Mateo (the "County"),
and the San Mateo County Superintendent of Schools has jurisdiction over the District;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE rr RESOLVED by the Board ofTtustees ofthe Pacifica School
Dish-ict as follows:
1. ffs Board of Trustees hereby finds and determines that foregoing recitals
are frue and correct.
2. Order of Election: Specifications of Ballot Measure. This resolution shall stand as the
order to the San Mateo County Superintendent of Schools to call an election within the boundaries
of the Distict on November 3, 2026, for the pumose of proposing to the electors of the Distict
the measure contained in Exhibit A hereto. The authority for the specifications of this
order is contained in Sections 5304 and 5322 of the California Educafion Code and Sections
50075-77 and 50079 of the California Govemment Code.
This Board of Trustees hereby requests the Regis&ar of Voters of the County of San Mateo
(the "Regisfrar of Voters") to submit to the voters of the Disfrict at said election the measure as it
appears in Exhibit A.
3. Filing ofOrder of ElecGon. The Secretary of this Board of Trustees is ordered to cause
certified copies of this resolution and order to be delivered not later than Wednesday, August 5,
2026, to the San Mateo County Superintendent of Schools, and not later than Friday, August 7,
2026, to the Registrar of Voters and the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors of the County.
4. Fonnal The San Mateo County Superintendent of Schools is hereby requested
to prepare and execute a Formal Notice of Parcel Tax Elecfion and consolidation order in
substantially the fom attached hereto as Exhibit B (the "Formal Notice"), and to call the election
by causing the Formal Notice to be posted in every schoolhouse in the District and at three public
places in the District, in accordance with Section 5362 of the Califomia Education Code, no later
than Wednesday, August 5, 2026, or to otherwise cause the noüce to be published as permitted by
law. The Secremry of this Board of Trustees, on behalf ofand as may be requested by the County
Superintendent of Schools, is authorized to cause all required by law in connection
herewith to be published and posted, as the case may be.
5. Conduct of Election. (a) Request to Registrar of Voters. Pursuant to Section 5303 of
the California Education Code, the Registrar of Voters is required to, and is hereby requested to,
take all steps to hold the election in accordance with law and these specifications.
(b) Ballot and Voter Pamphlet. The Registrar of Voters is requested to cause the exact
wording of the Abbreviation of the Measure contained in Exhibit A-I to appear on the ballot, and
to print the Full Text of the Measure contained in Exhibit A-II in the voter information pamphlet
to be distibuted to voters pursuant to the California Elections Code, The ftlll text of the measure
is all that text in Appendix A hereto between the indicators "BEGmNING OF FULL TEXT OF
MEASURE
END OF FULL TEXT OF MEASURE."
(c) Consolidation. The San Mateo County Superintendent of Schools and the Board of
Supervisors of the County are requested to order consolidation of the election with such other
elections as may be held on the same day in the same territory or in territory that is in part the
same, pursuant to California Education Code Section 5342 and Secfion 10400 and following of
the California Elections Code.
(d) Canvass of Results. The Board of Supervisors of the County is authorized to canvass
the returns of the election pursuant to Secfion 10411 of the California Elections Code.
(e) Required Vote. The proposition shall become effective upon approval of two-thirds of
those voting thereon.
(f) Election Costs. This Board of Trustees shall pay all costs of the elecHon approved by
the Board of Supervisors of the County, pursuant to California Education Code Section 5421.
6. Appropriations Limit. This Board of Trustees shall provide in each year (pursuant to
Section 7902.1 of the California Government Code or any successor provision of law) for any
increase in the District's appropriafions limit as shall be necessary to ensure that proceeds of the
proposed tax may be spent for the authorized purposes.
7. Ballot Argument, The President of this Board of Trustees, or any member or members
of this Board as the President shall designate, is hereby authorized, but not directed, to prepare and
file with the Registrar of Voters a ballot argument in favor of the proposifion contained in Exhibit
A-II hereof, within the time established by the Regisfrar of Voters, which shall be considered the
offcial ballot argument of this Board as sponsor of the proposition.
8. Effective Date. This resolution shall take effect from and after iG adoption by a two-
thirds vote of all of the members of this Board.

FORMAL NOTICE OF EDUCATION PARCEL TAX ELECTION
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN to the qualified electors of the Pacifica School
District of San Mateo County, California, that in accordance with the provisions of the Education

held on November 3, 2026, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified electors of the District
the proposition summarized as follows:
"To renew expiring local funding without increasing taxes, with
local funding for elementary/middle schools the state cannot take
away, to support strong math, science, history, reading/writing
programs; attract/retain qualified teachers/counselors; maintain
art/music/outdoor education programs, libraries and computer
instruction, shall Pacifica School District's measure be adopted,
levying $118 per parcel, raising $1,300,000 annually for 10 years,
with senior exemptions, independent oversight and no money for
administrator salaries?"

The County Superintendent of Schools of San Mateo County, by this Notice of

11. FULL TEXT OF THE PAEASURE
BEGINNING OF FULL TEXT OF MEASURE
PACmCA SCHOOL DISTRICT
PACIFICA QUALITY EDUCATION AND TEACHER RETENTION hffASIJRE
This Proposition may be known and referred to as the "Pacifica Quality Educafion
and Teacher Retention Measure" (the "Act") or as "Measure
[designation to be assigned
by County Registrar of Voters]
KEY FNDNGS
The Pacifica School Disfrict (the "Disfricf') is determined to provide excellent educational
programs to all its students. Nationally, California places near the bottom of the 50 states in
educational funding. The District is one of the lowest funded school disfricts in the county, and its
schools are sfruggling to recruit the best teachers to its classrooms. Having a quality teacher in
each classroom is one of the most important elements of a quality education, the District is
committed to attacting and retaining excellent teachers, counselors and staff. The District
achowledges the importance of paying teachers and other educational staff a living wage so they
can continue to live in the community where they work.
It is essenfial the Distict have stable, reliable local funding to maintain and improve its
quality educational programs and remains committed to attracfrg and retaining excellent teachers.
The Disfrict acknowledges the importance of paying teachers and other educational staff enough
money so they can continue to live in the community where they work. To better attract and retain
excellent teachers and other school educational suff, the Dis&ict wishes to ensure it can provide
competffve salaries.
On June 7, 2016, Pacifica voters renewed a school parcel tax measure ("Measure D") to
provide stable local funding to retain quality teachers, maintain smaller class sizes and protect
academic programs, preparing students to succeed in high school, college and 21 st century careers.
The existing parcel tax authorized by Measure D will expire as of June 30, 2027.
To provide a locally controlled funding that cannot be taken by the state, the District
has placed on the ballot the Pacifica Quality Education and Teacher Retention Measure, which
would impose a total of $118 in taxes per parcel annually for a period of ten years, with an
exemption available for senior citizens, and to implement accountability measures, including
cfizen oversight, to ensure the funds are used to help:
Enhance core academic programs like math, science, history, reading and writing;
Support outstanding music and electives crifical to a well-rounded education;
Attact and retain qualified teachers and staff,
Maintain classroom computer and technology instuction;
Strengthen school library programs; and
Maintain programs to support struggling students.
TERMS OF SPECIAL TAX
Terms. Upon approval of two-thirds of those voting on this measure, the District shall be
authorized to extend the existing parcel tax (Pacifica School District Parcel Tax of 2016) for ten
(10) years until 2037. The net effect of this measure would be to authorize the District to impose
a total of $118 in taxes per parcel annually each year between July 1, 2027, and June 30, 2037,
subject to an annual adjustment for inflation pursuant to the "Consumer Price Index for all Urban
Consumers San Francisco Area" published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor
In the event this index is no longer published, the Board of Trustees shall adopt a
comparable index of general price levels, as it shall reasonably determine.
Senior Citizen Exemption. In order to provide tax relief to senior citizens in the community,
any parcel owned and occupied by a person 65 years of age or older shall be exempt from the Act
upon proper application to the District The exemption shall be available pursuant to procedures
to be prescribed by the Disfrict's Board of Trustees or otherwise as required by law or by the San
Mateo County Tax Collector.
Additional Legal Exemptions. An exemption from the Funding for the Act shall be made
for persons receiving Supplemenml Security Income for a disability, regardless of age upon proper
application to the District. An exemption from the Act shall be made for persons receiving Social
Security Disability Insurance benefits, regardless of age, whose yearly income does not exceed
250 percent of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines issued by the United States Department of
Health and Human Services. These exemptions shall be available pursuant to procedures to be
prescribed by the Disfrict's Board of Trustees or otherwise as required by law or by the San Mateo
County Tax Collector.
ACCOUNTABILITY PROVISIONS
Annual Audit. Upon the levy and of the Act, the Board of Trustees shall cause
an account to be established for deposit of the proceeds. For so long as any proceeds of the Act
shall remain unexpended, the Superintendent or chief financial offcer of the Disfrict shall cause a
report to be filed with the Board of Trustees no later than December 31 of each year, commencing
December 31 , 2027, (1) the amount of Act received and expended in such year, and (2) the
status of any projects or description of any programs funding from proceeds of the tax. The report
may relate to the calendar year, fiscal year, or other appropriate annual period, as the
Superintendent shall determine and may be incorporated into or filed with the annual budget, audit,
or other appropriate roufine report to the Board of Trustees.
Independent Citizen Oversight Committee. The Board shall provide for the Distict's
Citizens' Oversight Committee to continue to oversee the special taxes collected pursuant
to the Act to ensure that moneys raised under the Act are spent only for the purposes described in
the Act. The Citizens' Oversight Committee shall continue to operate pursuant to its current
requirements regarding composition, duties, funding and other applicable protocols regarding the
Committee's formation and operation.
Specific Purposes. All of the purposes named in the measure shall constitute the specific
purposes of the Act, and proceeds of the tax shall be applied only for such purposes.
Appropriations Limit. The Board of Trustees shall provide in each year (pursuant to
Section 7902.1 of the Califomia Govemment Code or any successor provision of law) for any
increase in the District's appropriations limit as shall be necessary to ensure that proceeds of the
Act, and of all qualified special taxes levied by the Disfrict, may be spent for the authorized
purposes and an election shall be conducted by the District for such purpose only if required by
the general laws of the State applicable to school district qualified special taxes. This provision
shall be deemed to be declaratory of existing procedures governing District expenditures.
LEVY AND COLLECTION
The Act shall be collected by the San Mateo County Treasurer-Tax Collector at the same
time and in the same manner and shall be subject to the same penalties as ad valorem propeØ,'
taxes collected by the Treasurer-Tax Collector. Unpaid taxes shall bear interest at the same rate as
the rate for unpaid ad valorem property taxes unfil paid. The collection ofthe Act shall not decrease
the funds available from other sources of the District in any period from the effective date hereof.
"Parcél of taxable real property" shall be defined as any unit ofreal property in the District,
which receives a separate tax bill for ad valorem property taxes from the San Mateo County
Treasurer-Tax Collector's Offce. All property, which is otherwise exempt from or on which are
levied no ad valorem property taxes in any year, shall also be exempt from the Act in such year.
Any parcel owned and occupied by the following taxpayers shall be exempt from the Act as
provided herein: persons who are 65 years of age or older as of July 1 of the year.
The District shall annually provide a list of parcels, which the Distict has approved, for a
senior and certain other legal exemptions from the Act as described above to the San Mateo County
tax colleÆon offcials. The San Mateo County Assessor's determination of exemption or relief for
any reason of any parcel from other than through such exemptions, shall be final and
binding for the purposes of the Act. Taxpayers wishing to challenge the County Assessor's
determination must do so under the procedures for correcting a misclassification of property
pursuant to Section 4876.5 of the California Revenue and Taxation Code or other applicable
procedures. Taxpayers seeking a refund of the Act paid shall follow the procedures applicable to
property tax refunds pursuant to the California Revenue and Taxation Code.
SEVERABILITY
The Board of Trustees hereby declares, and the voters, by approving this measure,
concur, that every secü)n, paragraph, sentence and clause of this measure has independent value,
and the Board of Trustees and the voters would have adopted each provision hereof regardless of
every other provision hereof. Upon approval of this measure by the voters, should any part be
found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid for any reason, all remaining parts hereof
shall remain in full force and effect to the fullest extent allowed by law.
